q: 1. Moment of inertia of a circular section about its diameter (d) is
explain: The standard formula for the area moment of inertia of a circle about its centroidal axis (diameter) is πd⁴ / 64.

q: 2. M.O.I. of a circular section of diameter d about an axis passing through its C.G. lying in the plane of the section is given by
explain: The Moment of Inertia of a circle about its diameter is πd⁴/64.

q: 3. The ratio of max deflections of a SS beam with an isolated central load and that of with a UDL over its entire length, is
explain: Deflection(Point) = WL³/48EI. Deflection(UDL) = 5WL³/384EI. The ratio is (1/48) / (5/384) = 8/5 = 24/15.

q: 4. If the width of a simply supported beam carrying an isolated load at its centre is doubled, the deflection... is changed by
explain: Since deflection is inversely proportional to I (and thus width b), doubling the width reduces the deflection to half (1/2).

q: 5. If the width b and depth d of a beam simply supported with a central load are interchanged, the deflection... will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Deflection 1 ∝ 1/(bd³). Deflection 2 ∝ 1/(db³). Ratio Δ2/Δ1 = (bd³) / (db³) = d²/b² = (d/b)².

q: 6. A cantilever beam is one which is
options: fixed at one end and free at the other end
supported on more than two supports
explain: The defining characteristic of a cantilever is the single fixed support that provides all the necessary stability.

q: 7. A continuous beam is one which is
options: fixed at one end and free at the other end
supported on more than two supports
explain: Any beam having three or more supports is classified as a continuous beam.

q: 8. The shear force diagram of a cantilever beam of length l and carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length will be
explain: The SF varies linearly from zero at the free end to wl at the fixed end, forming a right-angled triangle.

q: 9. The bending moment of a cantilever beam of length l and carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is... at the fixed end.
explain: The total load is 'wl' acting at its center of gravity (l/2 from the support). Moment = (wl) * (l/2) = wl²/2.

q: 10. The bending moment in the centre of a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is
explain: The reaction is wl/2. BM at center = (wl/2 * l/2) - (w * l/2 * l/4) = wl²/4 - wl²/8 = wl²/8.

q: 11. The shear force at the centre of a simply supported beam with a gradually varying load from zero at both ends to w per metre at the centre, is
explain: Due to the symmetry of the triangular loading (zero at ends, max at center), the shear force at the exact mid-point of the span must be zero.

q: 12. When shear force at a point is zero, then bending moment is... at that point.
explain: Mathematically, V = dM/dx. If the derivative (V) is zero, the function (M) is at a local maximum or minimum.

q: 13. A cantilever beam carrying a uniformly distributed load W over its full length is propped at its free end... BM will be zero at its free end also at
explain: For a propped cantilever with UDL, the point of zero bending moment (contraflexure) occurs at a distance of 3/4L from the fixed end (or 1/4L from the prop).

q: 14. The bending moment in a beam will be maximum where
explain: The maximum bending moment occurs at the section where the shear force is zero or changes its sign.

q: 15. A simply supported beam is subjected to a uniformly varying load with zero intensity at the two ends increasing to W/m at the centre. the maximum S.F. is
explain: The total load is (1/2 * l * w). Since the loading is symmetrical, each reaction (Max SF) is half the total load: (1/2 * wl/2) = wl/4.

q: 16. the shape of the bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, having no external load, is always
explain: With no external load between two points, the shear force is constant (horizontal line), making the bending moment linear (inclined line).

q: 17. The bending moment is maximum on a section where shearing force
explain: According to the relationship dM/dx = V, the bending moment (M) reaches a local maximum or minimum value where the shear force (V) is zero or changes its sign.

q: 18. In a continuous bending moment curve the point where it changes sign, is called
explain: The point where the bending moment changes from sagging (+) to hogging (-) or vice versa is known by all these terms; it is the location where the curvature of the beam changes.

q: 19. In a three hinged arch, the third hinge is generally kept at
options: midpoint of the crown and left support hinge
midpoint of the crown and right support hinge
explain: To maintain symmetry and structural efficiency, the internal hinge is usually placed at the highest point of the arch, known as the crown.

q: 20. For a circular section Izz = Ixx = Iyy. Then zz-axis
options: will be tangential to the circle
will be passing through point of intersection... and perpendicular to the plane
explain: Izz represents the polar moment of inertia, which is the sum of Ixx and Iyy (Perpendicular Axis Theorem), passing through the centroid perpendicular to the section.

q: 21. If the section modulus of a beam is increased, the bending stress in the beam will
explain: Since σ = M/Z, bending stress is inversely proportional to the section modulus. A higher Z indicates a stronger section with lower stress for the same moment.

q: 22. When a cantilever beam is loaded at its free end, the maximum compressive stress shall develop at
explain: In a cantilever beam loaded downwards, the top fibers undergo tension (stretching) and the bottom fibers undergo compression (shortening).

q: 23. A cantilever beam of span 4 m and carrying a point load of 10 KN located at 3 m from the fixed end. Find the BM at the fixed and free end
explain: BM at fixed end = 10×3 = 30 kN-m; BM at the free end of any cantilever is always zero.

q: 24. The relation between the radius of curvature (R), bending moment (M) and flexural rigidity (EI) is given by
explain: From the bending equation: M/I = E/R, so M = EI/R.

q: 25. The variation of the bending moment in the segment of a beam where the load is uniformly distributed is
explain: Under UDL, shear varies linearly and bending moment (its integral) varies parabolically.

q: 26. The point of contraflexure occurs in a beam
explain: Contraflexure points typically arise in overhanging beams (and continuous beams), where sagging and hogging regions meet.

q: 27. The maximum bending moment caused by a moving load on a simply supported beam is
explain: For a single moving point load, the maximum BM occurs directly under the load at its critical position.

q: 28. In a simply supported beam with span L subjected to a point load W at center, find the maximum bending moment induced in the beam
explain: M_max = WL/4 for a central point load on a simply supported beam.

q: 29. Determinate beam can be analyzed with the help of
explain: A statically determinate beam can be fully solved using the three equations of static equilibrium (ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, ΣM=0).

q: 30. A beam fixed at both ends with a central load W in the middle will have zero bending moment at
explain: A fixed-fixed beam with central point load develops two points of contraflexure (zero BM), symmetric about mid-span.

q: 31. The maximum bending moment caused on a simply supported beam subjected to two equal concentrated loads (W/2) spaced at equal distance (L/3) over the span is
explain: For this standard two-point-load arrangement at the third-points, max BM = WL/6.

q: 32. The maximum deflection of a beam occurs at
explain: Maximum deflection occurs where the slope of the elastic curve (dy/dx) is zero.

q: 33. If the length of a simply supported beam carrying a concentrated load at the centre is doubled, the deflection at the center will become
explain: Since δ ∝ L³, doubling the span increases deflection by a factor of 2³ = 8.

q: 34. The diagram showing the variation of BM along the span of a beam is called
explain: By definition, a Bending Moment Diagram (BMD) plots BM variation along the span. (Double-check this against your printed key — some editions mismark this answer.)

q: 35. The slope of curve of B.M. diagram at any section will be equal to
options: the slope of loading at that section
the slope of shear force diagram at that section
the ordinate of shear force diagram at that section
the area of shear force diagram starting from any one end
explain: Since dM/dx = V, the slope of the BM curve at any point equals the SF value (ordinate) there.

q: 36. BM in a cantilever beam having span 1.8m and uniformly distributed load of 4kg/m
37. A point where SF is zero, BM is
explain: Where SF=0, BM reaches a local extremum — this could be either a maximum (sagging peak) or minimum (hogging peak) depending on the loading.

q: 38. The rate of change of shear force is called
explain: dV/dx = -w — the rate of change of shear force equals the load intensity.

q: 39. At the point of application of a concentrated load on a beam, there is
options: sudden change of slope of BM
explain: A point load causes a sudden jump (discontinuity) in the shear force diagram, which produces a sudden change in the slope of the BM diagram at that point.

q: 40. A cantilever beam is the one which is supported with
options: one end hinge and other on rollers
one end fixed and other on rollers
one end fixed and the other free
explain: A cantilever has one fixed end providing full restraint, and a completely free other end.

q: 41. The ratio of moment of inertia of a square section to that of a circular section for a given depth is given by
explain: For the same depth (square side = circle diameter), the square section has more material further from the axis, giving I_square/I_circle > 1.

q: 42. The amount of shear force at the maximum bending moment is
explain: Since dM/dx = V, bending moment is maximum where shear force is zero (i.e. minimum).

q: 43. Find the maximum BM induced in a simply supported beam if the beam is subjected to a point load of 4 KN at the centre of beam and span of the beam is 4 m
44. Find the maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam loaded with a UDL of 2 t/m having span 4m
45. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load W. The maximum bending moment, M is:
explain: M_max = WL/8 for a full-span UDL (W = total load) on a simply supported beam.

q: 46. Moment of inertia of an object having rectangular section of 'b' as width and 'd' as depth is given by
explain: Standard formula: I = bd³/12 about the centroidal axis.
